title: Rabi sunflower based cropping systems in Telangana for climate resilience and profitability
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Rabi sunflower based cropping systems in Telangana offer superior climate resilience and economic returns under receding soil moisture conditions. Cultivation of short-duration rabi sunflower following early-harvested kharif legumes or green manure enhances system water productivity. Sowing during late October to mid-November optimizes flowering under favorable temperatures and avoids terminal heat stress. Ensures higher oil content and remunerative net returns in semi-arid tracts of Telangana.

title: Profitable cropping systems with broad bed & furrow and ridge-furrow configuration for Vertisols
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Land configuration using Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) and ridge-furrow layouts in black cotton soils (Vertisols) effectively mitigates both waterlogging during heavy rainfall and moisture deficit during extended dry spells. BBF beds of 105 cm width with 45 cm furrows facilitate drainage of excess runoff while improving rainwater infiltration. Intercropping cotton or soybean with pigeonpea under BBF layout increases rainfed crop yields by 18-22% and prevents root rot caused by transient water stagnation.

title: Contour farming technology for conserving soil moisture and productivity enhancement in rainfed crops grown on Alfisols in Central Telangana Zone
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Contour farming and vegetative contour barrier technology conserve in-situ rainwater and soil fertility in undulating red gravelly Alfisols across the Central Telangana Zone (Warangal district). Ploughing and sowing strictly across the slope along contour guide lines slows down surface runoff, reduces topsoil erosion by over 40%, and prolongs root-zone moisture availability by 10 to 14 days during dry spells, stabilizing yields of rainfed cotton, maize, and redgram.

title: Identification of suitable mustard varieties for Central and Northern Telangana Zones
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Evaluation and identification of thermo-tolerant, high-yielding Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) varieties for rabi cultivation in Central and Northern Telangana. Mustard provides a viable low-water alternative to rabi paddy. Timely sowing in late October ensures vegetative development before winter fog and aphid incidence, producing seed yields of 12-15 quintals per hectare with only 2-3 protective irrigations.

title: Yield potential of sunhemp genotypes under different sowing windows in Northern Telangana Zone
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Sunhemp (Crotalaria juncea) genotypes evaluated across varied sowing windows demonstrated superior green biomass and soil incorporation benefits in Northern Telangana. Sowing with pre-monsoon showers in early June produces over 20 tonnes of green biomass per hectare within 45 to 50 days, sequestering biological nitrogen and enhancing subsequent crop performance while improving soil organic matter.

title: Optimal sowing window and sowing method in Dry Direct Seeded Rice (D DSR)
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Dry Direct Seeded Rice (D-DSR) established with precision machinery serves as a climate-resilient alternative to traditional flooded transplanting. The optimal sowing window is 10 to 15 days prior to the onset of the southwest monsoon or immediately upon first pre-monsoon rains (late May to mid-June). Seeds must be drilled at a shallow depth of 2 to 3 cm using a tractor-drawn seed-cum-fertilizer drill or zero-till seed drill into well-prepared dry tilth. D-DSR saves 30-40% irrigation water, eliminates nursery raising and transplanting labour drudgery, and allows the crop to mature 7-10 days earlier, avoiding terminal irrigation shortages.

title: Soil test based fertilizer recommendation for targeted yield in sugarcane (Plant Crop)
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Soil Test Crop Response (STCR) correlation equations for plant sugarcane calibrate precise nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium requirements based on initial soil test values for specific yield targets (100 to 140 t/ha). STCR calibration eliminates over-fertilization, lowers production costs, and improves cane stalk thickness and juice sucrose purity.

title: Soil test based fertilizer recommendation for targeted yield in sugarcane (Ratoon Crop)
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Targeted yield fertilizer prescription equations for ratoon sugarcane in Telangana. Ratoon crops demand rapid nitrogen and potassium assimilation following stubble shaving and trash management. Application according to STCR equations enhances tiller survival, prevents early senescence, and achieves targeted millable cane yields economically.

title: Soil test based fertilizer prescription equations for targeted yield of Bt cotton in Alfisols
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Soil Test Crop Response (STCR) fertilizer prescription equations formulated specifically for Bt cotton grown on red sandy loam and chalka soils (Alfisols) in the Central Telangana Zone (Warangal). Equations account for native soil nutrient supply to achieve target yields of 25 to 30 quintals of seed cotton per hectare. Split application of nitrogen and potassium at squaring, peak flowering, and boll development stages maximizes boll weight and avoids square shedding caused by luxury or deficient vegetative growth.

title: Soil test based prescription equations for balanced fertilizer use and targeted yield of Bt cotton in Vertisols
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: STCR-based balanced fertilizer prescription equations for Bt cotton on deep black cotton soils (Vertisols). Nutrient prescription based on targeted yield equations balances nitrogen with potassium and phosphorus, curbing excessive vegetative canopy expansion common in heavy black soils. Enhances light penetration into the mid-canopy, minimizes internal boll rot, and increases net farm income through judicious fertilizer expenditure.

title: Sulphur and boron fertilization for yield maximisation of groundnut grown on Alfisols
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Secondary and micronutrient management in groundnut cultivated on light-textured Alfisols. Application of sulphur through gypsum at pegging stage combined with soil-applied or foliar boron significantly reduces blind nuts (pop pods), improves pod filling, and enhances oil content by 2-3 percentage points.

title: Integrated plant nutrient supply system in greengram-sorghum sequential cropping system under rainfed conditions
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Integrated plant nutrient supply (IPNS) combining farmyard manure (FYM), biofertilizers (Rhizobium and PSB), and balanced mineral fertilizers in a rainfed greengram followed by rabi sorghum sequential system. Inoculation and organic manuring leave residual nitrogen for the succeeding sorghum crop, improving soil health and stabilizing system productivity.

title: Enhancing production potential of pigeonpea through foliar nutrition
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Foliar nutrition interventions in rainfed pigeonpea (redgram) during critical reproductive phases. Supplemental foliar sprays at flower initiation and 15 days later reduce flower drop, improve pod setting on secondary branches, and increase seed yield by 12-16% under soil moisture stress conditions.

title: Nitrogen management in dry converted wet rice system
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Management of dry-converted wet rice (semi-dry rice) where rice is initially seeded dry under rainfed conditions due to delayed irrigation releases and subsequently converted to wet flooded ecology upon canal or tank water arrival. Nitrogen should be managed in split applications, withholding major nitrogen until flooding begins, followed by splits at active tillering and panicle initiation. Prevents severe denitrification and leaching losses while ensuring healthy tillering and robust panicle development in Telangana command areas.

title: Optimizing nitrogen and potassium application for rabi sunflower through fertigation
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Drip fertigation scheduling for nitrogen and potassium in rabi sunflower. Supplying soluble fertilizers in weekly splits matched to crop growth stages improves nutrient use efficiency by 25-30% compared to conventional soil dressing, resulting in larger head diameter, higher seed weight, and substantial water conservation.

title: Drip irrigation regimes and fertigation schedules in rabi cauliflower
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Standardized drip irrigation and fertigation protocol for rabi cauliflower. Scheduling irrigation at 0.8 ETc with split fertigation yields compact, uniform, snow-white curds with higher marketable recovery while saving 35% water over furrow irrigation.

title: Water budgeting of irrigated lowland rice using drum culture technique
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Water budgeting and monitoring in puddled lowland rice using micro-lysimeter and drum culture techniques. Farmers are advised to avoid continuous deep flooding (5-10 cm) throughout the season. Maintaining shallow water depth (2-3 cm) during vegetative tillering and panicle initiation, followed by intermittent drainage until hairline crack formation, conserves 25% irrigation water without any reduction in grain yield in the Central Telangana Zone.

title: Water budgeting of Alternate Wetting and Drying rice (AWD) with drum culture Technique
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) water management in rice monitored through field water tubes (pani pipes). A 30 cm long perforated plastic pipe is installed in the paddy field with 20 cm below the soil surface. Irrigation is re-applied only when the water level inside the pipe drops to 15 cm below the soil surface during vegetative stages. Continuous flooding is retained only from flowering to milk stage. AWD saves 25 to 35% irrigation water, improves root aeration, reduces lodging, and decreases methane greenhouse gas emissions significantly.

title: Weed management in rice – maize cropping system under conservation agriculture
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Weed management strategies in rice-maize cropping systems managed under zero tillage and conservation agriculture. Stale seedbed preparation prior to sowing followed by mechanical inter-cultivation with power weeders or manual spot weeding effectively suppresses troublesome grassy weeds (Echinochloa colona) and sedges (Cyperus rotundus). Retaining crop residue mulch creates a physical barrier that delays weed emergence, promotes beneficial microflora, and conserves residual soil moisture.

title: Non-chemical weed management in okra-carrot organic cropping system
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Non-chemical weed suppression in vegetable crop sequences combining organic mulches (paddy straw, dried leaves) and shallow mechanical weeding with hand hoes. Effective weed suppression was achieved during critical first 30 days without synthetic herbicides, maintaining organic product purity and soil biological activity.

title: Agronomic package for selective mechanisation in cotton on rainfed Alfisols
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Comprehensive agronomic package for selective mechanization in rainfed cotton grown on red sandy loam soils (Alfisols) in the Central Telangana Zone (Warangal). Synchronized package utilizes tractor-drawn inclined plate planters for precise geometry, followed by mini-tractor or power-weeder inter-cultivators at 20-25 and 40-45 days after sowing (DAS). Boom sprayers ensure rapid, uniform canopy coverage against pest flare-ups. Selective mechanization saves 40 to 45 man-days of labour per hectare, eliminates production bottlenecks during peak weeding and spraying, and boosts seed cotton yields by 15-20%.

title: Agronomic package for complete mechanisation in pigeonpea on rainfed Alfisols
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Complete mechanization package for rainfed pigeonpea on Alfisols covering mechanized seedbed preparation, pneumatic planter sowing, mechanical inter-row weeding, and combine harvesting with modified reel attachments. Overcomes severe farm labor shortages, reduces cultivation costs by 30%, and prevents harvest shattering losses.

title: Selective mechanization for safflower growers profitability
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Selective mechanization solutions for safflower cultivation addressing the major constraint of spiny plants during inter-cultivation and harvesting. Tractor-mounted multi-crop planters and specialized thresher units enhance harvest efficiency, eliminate painful manual drudgery, and improve marketability of clean seed.

title: Machine transplanting and direct seeding of rice are the best options over conventional transplanting in puddled soils
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Evaluation of motorized mechanical transplanting and drum seeding in puddled rice soils in Telangana. Mechanical transplanting using 4-row or 8-row self-propelled transplanters with 15-day-old mat nursery seedlings ensures uniform hill spacing (30 x 12 cm or 30 x 14 cm) with 30-33 hills per square meter. Eliminates bending drudgery for farm labourers, reduces transplanting costs by 40-50%, ensures faster seedling establishment with minimal root shock, and increases paddy grain yield by 8-12% compared to haphazard manual transplanting.

title: Quick cooking redgram dhal – A convenience product
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Post-harvest technology protocol for processing quick-cooking redgram (pigeonpea) dhal developed by PJTSAU. Controlled pre-treatment and thermal puffing techniques reduce domestic boiling and cooking time from 35 minutes down to 10-12 minutes, conserving fuel energy while retaining high protein and dietary fiber content.

title: Management of stem borer in rice with novel insecticides
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) guidelines for yellow stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas) in rice in Telangana. Cultural controls include clipping seedling leaf tips prior to transplanting to eliminate egg masses, synchronizing transplanting within communities, and installing pheromone traps at 8 to 10 traps per hectare for monitoring. Chemical intervention is warranted only when field monitoring reveals pest populations exceeding economic threshold levels (ETL): 10% dead hearts at vegetative stage or 2% white ears at flowering stage. Farmers must refer to approved product labels for specific registered formulations, timing, and dosage, and consult the nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or Kisan Call Centre (1551) before spraying.

title: Novel insecticide combinations for the control of sucking pests and pink bollworm in cotton
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategy for pink bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) and sucking insect complexes (jassids, aphids, thrips, whiteflies) in Bt cotton across the Central Telangana Zone (Warangal). Cultural management involves erecting yellow sticky traps for sucking pests, installing pink bollworm pheromone traps at 5 traps per acre starting 45 days after sowing (DAS), and detopping/nipping terminal shoots at 80-90 DAS to remove favoured oviposition sites. Manually collect and destroy rosette flowers containing larvae. Chemical sprays should be initiated only when trap catches exceed 8 moths per trap per day for three consecutive days or 10% damaged green bolls with live larvae. Farmers must strictly follow instructions on registered product labels and seek guidance from local KVK or Call Centre (1551) for approved molecules, dosages, and safe handling precautions.

title: Novel fungicide molecules to manage anthracnose disease in soybean
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Management of anthracnose / pod blight (Colletotrichum truncatum) in soybean in Northern Telangana. Field sanitation, crop rotation with non-host cereals, and certified disease-free seed selection are primary defenses. Follow registered product labels and consult local agricultural extension officers or KVK for verified fungicide treatments and dosage.

title: Use of nuclear polyhedrosis virus (SNPV) and bird perches to reduce insect pests in bhendi
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Eco-friendly biological pest management in okra (bhendi) using Spodoptera Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus (SNPV) combined with erecting bird perches (T-shaped bamboo perches at 20 per acre). Encourages predatory insectivorous birds and utilizes targeted biological viral solutions, significantly reducing synthetic pesticide usage and chemical residues in harvest.

title: Seed treatment with copper oxychloride / azadirachtin to reduce bird damage at sowing stage in maize and sunflower
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Seed deterrence treatment protocols to repel birds during germination and early seedling emergence in maize and sunflower. Treating seed with registered botanical bitter repellents or seed dressing forms a gustatory repellent that protects newly sprouted seeds from parakeets, crows, and pigeons, ensuring uniform plant stand establishment in open fields.

title: Planting barrier crops to reduce bird damage in maize crop
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Border barrier cropping technique using tall, non-palatable boundary crops (such as castor or forage sorghum) around maize plots. The vegetative barrier obstructs line-of-sight flight paths of destructive bird flocks, reducing damage to outer maize cobs by over 50% without harming avian wildlife.

title: Integrated bird management in maize using reflective ribbons and wrapping method
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Integrated physical bird scaring technology utilizing multi-colored reflective holographic ribbons strung above the crop canopy combined with mechanical husk wrapping. Wind-induced ribbon fluttering and light reflection disorient bird flocks during cob maturity, protecting high-value seed production plots cost-effectively.

title: Block plantation, reflective ribbons and whole egg solution spray in sunflower and bajra to reduce bird damage
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Multi-tactic bird management in sunflower and pearl millet (bajra) combining compact block plantations, border reflective ribbons, and spraying biological repellent solutions (whole egg formulation) on boundary rows during seed development. Deters bird flocks through olfactory and visual signals, preserving sunflower capitulum seed fill.

title: Management of Macrophomina phaseolina stem and root rot of sesame
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Cultural and biological management of stem and charcoal root rot (Macrophomina phaseolina) in sesame. Soil incorporation of Trichoderma viride enriched farmyard manure combined with deep summer ploughing and balanced irrigation prevents dry root rot outbreaks in sandy loam soils during high temperature spells.

title: Soybean storage technology: Impact on quality and health of treated seeds
publisher: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU)
raw_text: Post-harvest seed handling and hermetic storage protocols for soybean in Northern Telangana. Maintaining seed moisture strictly below 9% and packing seeds in multi-layer hermetic bags (PICS bags) or polythene-lined containers preserves germination vigor above 70% across 8 months of storage, preventing seed coat cracking and mycoflora deterioration.
